slides.title: If Statement Basics
slides.content: An if statement runs code only when a condition is true. The condition must evaluate to a bool.

exercise.prompt: When does an if block execute?

slides.title: If-Else
slides.content: The else block provides an alternative path when the if condition is false.

slides.title: Else If
slides.content: Use else if to chain multiple conditions. They are checked in order until one is true.

exercise.prompt: The keyword for additional conditions is _____

slides.title: Nested Conditions
slides.content: You can place an if inside another if to check multiple related conditions.

exercise.prompt: Print 'Special' only when both isMember and isVIP are true
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: if, Console.WriteLine
When run, your code should output: Special

slides.title: Ternary Operator
slides.content: The ternary operator is a compact if-else for simple assignments or returns.

slides.title: Boolean Conditions
slides.content: Conditions can be bool variables, comparisons, or method calls that return bool.

exercise.prompt: Which of these is a valid condition?

slides.title: Switch Expression Basics
slides.content: Switch expressions evaluate an input and return a result based on matching patterns. They use the => syntax.

slides.title: Best Practices
slides.content: Keep conditions simple and readable. Use braces for all blocks to avoid errors. Prefer switch expressions over long else if chains.

slides.title: Flow Builder: If-Else
slides.content: Use the Flow Builder to create an if-else that prints 'Pass' or 'Fail'.

exercise.prompt: Build a flow that declares int score = 75, then if score >= 60 outputs 'Pass' else outputs 'Fail'
